correctness.rationale: Both directions of the exact coefficient formula are proved. Nonzero coefficient products are realized with positive simplex weights using a continuous scalar energy reaching 1, covering strict interior/boundary, one-point support and zero separately. Equality in triangle inequalities gives the rank-three phase-affine-independence characterization of extreme points; Krein–Milman in finite dimension yields three-site generation; an explicit three-phase coefficient vector yields sharpness for every |q|<1. The 1943 successful reproducibility cases supplement, not replace, the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge originality comparison: the motivating arXiv:2610.32504 theorem gives continuous q ranges and a unimodular-q realization, including necessary l1 estimates in one diagonal construction, but not this full coefficient feasibility at strict interior q. arXiv:2410.03669 establishes commuting tuple convexity only in dimension two. The scalar Chien–Nakazato three-eigenvalue theorem does not itself imply simultaneous range equality or coefficient extreme classification. Exact searches of accessible prior records and the local claim ledger produced no matching result. Residual possible implicit older convex-geometry formulation is disclosed.

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies the geometry for the natural simultaneously normal finite-dimensional subclass of recently defined function-valued joint q ranges, in sharp contrast with the generally nonconvex case. The explicit complex l1 slice, all extreme coefficient phases, and universal optimal three-site convexification constitute a motivated structural classification, usable for arbitrary families and tuple lengths, rather than a routine bound or arbitrary finite example.
